about.title: Lafayette Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary day in Lafayette into a serious injury — whether it's a faulty auto part that fails along SR-24, a malfunctioning household appliance, or a tool that breaks during normal use. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person typically doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. Liability can extend beyond the manufacturer to distributors and retailers who put the product into commerce. Contra Costa County residents dealing with a defective-product injury often face medical bills, lost income, and confusion about who's actually responsible. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects you with an independent attorney who can evaluate the product, the defect, and your options. If a product is involved, keep it — don't repair, discard, or alter it, since it's often the most important piece of evidence in these claims.

whyChoose.title: Why Lafayette Residents Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path Forward
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. That can make a claim more direct than other injury cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. An attorney can help identify which parties were involved in getting the product to you.

items.title: Free Connection, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: LawProactive doesn't charge for connecting you with an attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency — no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury — don't clean, repair, or discard it. In product liability cases, the item itself is often the central piece of evidence showing the defect. If possible, store it somewhere safe and take photos before moving it.

items.question: Does a defective product injury near SR-24 change anything about my claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily — what matters most is the product itself and how it failed, not the road or location where the injury happened. Lafayette's SR-24 corridor sees a fair number of injury collisions, but a product defect claim focuses on the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer, not traffic patterns.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability approach usually means you only need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company acted carelessly or knew about the problem. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your specific case.
